raw_response:
I'm 70 years old now, been working this land for 40 years. My wife and I only have 2.6 mu, not much, but it's what we've got. I only finished primary school, so I don't know all those book formulas, but I know this soil and I know what works. We don't have much cash lying around — just my small pension and what the crops bring in — so every yuan I spend has to count.

**Winter wheat** — I always plant around the middle of October, same as everyone in the village. Last year I got about 400 jin per mu, which was decent. My neighbor Old Wang said his wheat looked good with the same variety we've been using, so I'll stick with that. I buy seed from the village supply store — costs about 30 yuan per mu. I don't have a tractor anymore, so I hire Zhang's boy to come rotary-till the field. That costs me but I can't do the heavy plowing myself at my age.

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu before planting — that's what I've always done. Then when the wheat turns green in spring and starts jointing, if it looks a bit yellow I topdress with urea. Last year I used about half a bag of urea per mu at jointing and it turned out fine, so I'll do the same. I know the young extension fellow says I should do soil tests, but I've been farming this plot long enough to see what it needs.

Water is expensive now with the electric pumps, but you can't skip it. I irrigate three times for wheat: once before winter so it doesn't dry out, once at jointing in March or April, and once when the heads are coming out. Three times is what most folks around here do, and I can't afford to lose yield by saving on water.

For pests, I spray herbicide once after planting to keep the weeds down. Sometimes the aphids come in spring, so I keep a small bottle of insecticide ready. I do the spraying myself — my wife helps mix the chemicals.

**Summer maize** — As soon as the wheat comes off in early June, I need to get the maize in the ground. The window is tight, maybe a week if I'm lucky. I plant hybrid seed — everyone uses hybrids now, you can't save your own maize seed anymore, it doesn't work. That seed costs more, about 45 yuan per mu, but it's worth it. I hire Zhang's tractor again to do a quick pass, then plant right away.

For maize fertilizer, I put compound fertilizer in the hole at planting, then add urea when the plants are knee-high. I don't go crazy with fertilizer — maybe a bit less than the big farms because I can't afford it — but I make sure the plants get enough. Last year I used about the same as always and got nearly 450 jin per mu.

Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat. I irrigate twice if it's dry — once right after planting if the soil is too dry for the seeds, and once when the tassels come out. If it rains enough, maybe only once. I watch the sky like everyone else.

My wife and I do most of the work ourselves — planting, fertilizing, watering, harvesting. It's hard work at our age, but what choice do we have? I might hire a couple of days of help for the wheat harvest and maybe one day for maize, especially if I'm feeling stiff in the back. All together, with just 2.6 mu, we can manage, but we have to go slow.

I'm expecting about 400 kg per mu for wheat and maybe 420 kg per mu for maize. Not the best in the village, but at my age with this small plot, I'm not trying to win prizes — I'm just trying to keep food on the table and have a little left to sell.
